authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Kiniksa raised its 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance to between $1.045 and $1.050 billion, up from the prior range of between $980 and $995 million.
The FDA approved Samsung Biologics as the replacement CDMO for ARCALYST drug substance manufacturing, following the technology transfer that Regeneron started.

Kiniksa announced that the pivotal Phase 3 trial of KPL-387 in recurrent pericarditis (PASTORALE) had begun enrolling and dosing patients. Data are expected in the second half of 2027, and commercialization is expected in 2028 or 2029.

business_model.claim: Kiniksa's only marketed product is ARCALYST, a cytokine trap licensed from Regeneron. It is sold in the United States, mainly for recurrent pericarditis, and substantially all revenue comes from the United States.
quotes: We are currently only authorized to market ARCALYST, our sole product, for the treatment of recurrent pericarditis in the United States, where we derive substantially all of our revenue.
We received FDA approval of ARCALYST for the treatment of recurrent pericarditis and reduction in risk of recurrence in adults and children 12 years and older in March 2021.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and 10-K MD&A
business_model.claim: Kiniksa sells ARCALYST through a third-party logistics provider and a select network of specialty pharmacies, which it calls its customers. The pharmacies deliver the drug to patients by mail. Revenue is booked net of discounts, rebates, chargebacks, copay assistance and similar adjustments.
quotes: ARCALYST is sold through a third party logistics provider that distributes primarily through a select network of specialty pharmacies
which deliver the medication to patients by mail.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and the earnings release table
business_model.claim: Reported revenue is entirely ARCALYST net product revenue. It was $285,970 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026 versus $180,855 in the third quarter of 2025, and $743,836 for the nine months of 2026 versus $475,437 for the nine months of 2025. No license and collaboration revenue was recorded in these periods.
quotes: Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $286.0 million, compared to $180.9 million for the third quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release and 10-K MD&A
business_model.claim: The main volume driver is patient adoption. About 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were on ARCALYST at the end of the third quarter of 2026. The 10-K attributed the 2025 and 2024 revenue increases primarily to patient enrollment.
quotes: As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, approximately 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were actively on ARCALYST treatment.
The increases in 2025 and 2024 were primarily driven by an increase in patient enrollment.

business_model.claim: Management raised its 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance to a range of $1.045 billion to $1.050 billion, from a prior range of $980 million to $995 million.
quotes: Kiniksa expects 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue of between $1.045 billion and $1.050 billion, compared to prior guidance of between $980 million and $995 million.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and MD&A and the 10-K MD&A
business_model.claim: The largest cost line is collaboration expense, which is Regeneron's share of ARCALYST profit. It was $105,828 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026 versus $63,307 a year earlier. It rises as ARCALYST sales rise.
quotes: We evenly split profits on sales of ARCALYST with Regeneron, where profits are determined after deducting from net sales of ARCALYST certain costs related to the manufacturing and commercialization of ARCALYST.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and earnings release
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold covers ARCALYST production and distribution, amortization of a milestone payment made to Regeneron, and technology-transfer labor and overhead. It was $27,759 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026 versus $20,257 a year earlier, and the earnings release says the increase was primarily due to costs associated with increased sales.
quotes: The increase in COGS expenses was primarily due to costs associated with increased sales of ARCALYST.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement and earnings release
business_model.claim: Operating spending outside collaboration expense and cost of goods sold is research and development and selling, general and administrative. R&D was $32,786 (table in thousands) versus $24,166 in the third quarter, with the increase due primarily to KPL-387 clinical activity. SG&A was $65,361 versus $49,104, with the increase due primarily to investment in ARCALYST commercialization.
quotes: The increase in R&D expenses was primarily due to increased KPL-387 clinical activity.
The increase in SG&A expenses was primarily due to investment associated with the commercialization of ARCALYST.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q income statement; the comparison of growth rates is inferred from the line items
business_model.claim: Income from operations was $54,236 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026 versus $24,021 a year earlier, and net income was $47,345 versus $18,435. Revenue growth exceeded the growth in operating costs in this period.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the absence of 2026 license revenue is read from the earnings release table
business_model.claim: Kiniksa also holds out-licences to Huadong (ARCALYST in the Huadong Territory) and Genentech (vixarelimab). They can add milestones and royalties, but no license revenue was recognised in the 2026 periods shown. About $570.0 million of Genentech contingent payments remained as of September 30, 2026.
quotes: Under the Genentech License Agreement, we will be eligible to receive up to a total of approximately $600.0 million in contingent payments, including specified development, regulatory and sales-based milestones, of which approximately $570.0 million remains as of September 30, 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the balance sheet, cash flow statement and earnings release
business_model.claim: Inventory more than doubled to $108,028 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026 from $54,895 at December 31, 2025. Operating cash flow for the nine months was $144,941, with cash and short-term investments of $568.8 million and no debt.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, Kiniksa had $568.8 million of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments and no debt.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and earnings release
business_model.claim: Future revenue and cost drivers include KPL-387, a monthly subcutaneous antibody for recurrent pericarditis now in a pivotal Phase 3 trial. Data are expected in the second half of 2027 and commercialization is targeted for 2028 or 2029. This is a development cost today and not yet a source of revenue.
quotes: We expect data from such trial in the second half of 2027.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (company's own description)
competitive_position.claim: ARCALYST has a first-mover position in recurrent pericarditis. The 10-K calls it the first and only FDA-approved therapy for the disease. Its dual IL-1α/IL-1β blockade is presented as a differentiator.
quotes: ARCALYST, a weekly, subcutaneously injected, recombinant fusion protein that blocks IL-1α and IL-1β signaling, is the first and only FDA-approved therapy for recurrent pericarditis.

competitive_position.claim: Sales are growing fast. Q3 2026 revenue was $285,970 (table in thousands) against $180,855 a year earlier, and management raised 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance to $1.045 - $1.050 billion. The prior-year 10-K attributed growth to more patient enrollment.
quotes: ARCALYST 2026 expected net product revenue increased to $1.045 - $1.050 billion
The increases in 2025 and 2024 were primarily driven by an increase in patient enrollment.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated in the items; the headroom reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Penetration of the target population is still modest, which implies room to grow. About 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were on ARCALYST at the end of Q3 2026. The 10-K also cites about 40,000 prevalent recurrent pericarditis patients in the US.
quotes: As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, approximately 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were actively on ARCALYST treatment.

competitive_position.claim: Prescriber reach is broad. More than 5,450 prescribers have written ARCALYST prescriptions for recurrent pericarditis since launch. The 10-K says guidance now places IL-1 inhibition as second-line therapy after first-line failure in the auto-inflammatory phenotype.
quotes: Since launch, more than 5,450 prescribers have written ARCALYST prescriptions for recurrent pericarditis.
which prioritized IL-1 inhibition therapy as a second-line treatment after failure of first-line therapy in the auto-inflammatory phenotype

competitive_position.basis: figures stated; the interpretation of collaboration expenses comes from the 10-Q MD&A description
competitive_position.claim: Operating leverage is visible, but Regeneron takes half of profits. Income from operations was $54,236 (table in thousands) against $24,021 a year earlier, while collaboration expenses, which are mainly Regeneron's profit share, were $105,828 on revenue of $285,970.
quotes: We are responsible for sales and distribution of ARCALYST in all approved indications in the United States and evenly split profits on sales as well as third party proceeds with Regeneron.

competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet is strong. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $568.8 million with no debt, and nine-month operating cash flow was $144,941 (table in thousands). This funds the commercial and pipeline spending that supports the competitive position.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, Kiniksa had $568.8 million of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments and no debt.

competitive_position.basis: timelines stated by the company; the franchise-defense reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: The follow-on asset KPL-387 is meant to defend and extend the franchise. It is a monthly subcutaneous IL-1R1 antibody in a pivotal trial (PASTORALE) with data expected in the second half of 2027 and commercialization expected in 2028 or 2029.
quotes: In addition, we announced that we expect to begin commercializing KPL-387 in 2028 or 2029.

competitive_position.basis: the approval and balances are stated; the link between the inventory build and the transition is inferred
competitive_position.claim: A threat: supply depends on a manufacturing transition away from Regeneron, and inventory has doubled. The FDA approved Samsung as replacement CDMO in June 2026, and inventory was $108,028 against $54,895 at year-end 2025 (table in thousands).
quotes: in June 2026 the FDA approved Samsung Biologics Co., Ltd.

competitive_position.claim: A threat: all revenue comes from one product in one country. The company calls ARCALYST its sole product and says substantially all revenue comes from the United States.
quotes: We are currently only authorized to market ARCALYST, our sole product, for the treatment of recurrent pericarditis in the United States, where we derive substantially all of our revenue.

competitive_position.basis: stated risk factors; no specific current payor action is documented
competitive_position.claim: A threat: payor and government pricing pressure, including biosimilars and lower-cost comparators. The 10-K names administration actions to limit drug prices and 'most favored nation' proposals.
quotes: In addition, the current presidential administration has taken and will likely continue to take action to limit or reduce the price of drugs and biologics.

Payors may adopt stricter coverage criteria or select lower-cost clinical comparators, including biosimilars or competitive products (with the same or similar indications), as benchmarks for making value/benefit assessments.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the risk factor; the licence dependence is described in Item 1
competitive_position.claim: A threat: ARCALYST depends on a licence from Regeneron, and the company relies on a select network of specialty pharmacies for distribution. Distribution failures or the loss of a pharmacy could disrupt patient therapy.
quotes: We rely on a select network of third party specialty pharmacies to market and sell ARCALYST that may not meet our or our patients’ needs.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the components are read directly from the 10-Q balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is large. The company reported $568.8 million of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments at the latest quarter-end, and states it has no debt. The balance sheet splits this into cash and equivalents of 81,660 and short-term investments of 487,098 (table in thousands).
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, Kiniksa had $568.8 million of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments and no debt.

financial_health.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q balance sheet; the link to the profit split is inferred from the MD&A description of collaboration expenses.
financial_health.claim: Current assets of 750,099 exceed current liabilities of 191,855 by a wide margin (table in thousands). Current assets rose from 527,177 at year-end, mainly because short-term investments, inventory and receivables grew.

financial_health.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q balance sheet; 'no debt' is stated in the release.
financial_health.claim: Financial leverage is low. Total liabilities are 273,050 against shareholders' equity of 710,193 (table in thousands), and the balance sheet shows no borrowings line. The liabilities are operating items: accruals, deferred revenue of 31,811, lease liabilities and other long-term liabilities of 45,469.
quotes: no debt

financial_health.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q cash flow statement; the mechanism is inferred from the reconciling lines.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash generation is positive and growing. Net cash provided by operating activities was 144,941 over nine months against 84,091 a year earlier (table in thousands), on net income of 95,369 (table in thousands). Capital expenditure was small at 1,004 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Figures are read from the statements; the low-cash-tax explanation is inferred from the tax lines and the deferred tax asset balance.

Cash taxes paid were only 9 against a provision of 27,514 (table in thousands), with deferred tax assets of 198,042 on the balance sheet. Other long-term liabilities added 26,857 to operating cash flow (table in thousands). Share-based compensation of 34,757 is a non-cash add-back.

financial_health.basis: Read directly from the cash flow statement and balance sheet; the redeployment reading is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Cash fell by 83,936 over nine months while short-term investments rose, because the company moved cash into investments rather than burning it (table in thousands). It purchased 457,156 of short-term investments and received 214,100 of maturities, so investing outflow was 244,060.

financial_health.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Financing flows are small and equity-related, with no debt issuance or repayment shown. Net cash from financing was 15,183, made up of 30,042 from share issuance under incentive plans less 14,859 paid for employee tax obligations on tendered shares (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cited items for the liquidity sufficiency, the guidance and the absence of debt; the lease amounts are read from the balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: No debt maturities or refinancing need appears in the evidence, because the company reports no debt. Management says its operating plan should stay cash flow positive on an annual basis. Operating needs are to be met from existing cash and investments plus ARCALYST sales. The annual report liquidity note says these resources are sufficient for at least twelve months.
quotes: Kiniksa expects its current operating plan to remain cash flow positive on an annual basis.

Based on its current operating plan, the Company expects that its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments combined with cash anticipated to be generated from sales of ARCALYST will be sufficient to fund its operations and capital expenditure requirements for at least twelve months from the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements.

financial_health.basis: Concentration and profit split are stated in the filings; the cash-flow implication is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation depends on one product in one market. ARCALYST is the sole product and the United States provides substantially all revenue. Half of ARCALYST profits go to Regeneron through collaboration expenses, which were 105,828 for the quarter against revenue of 285,970 (table in thousands).
quotes: We are currently only authorized to market ARCALYST, our sole product, for the treatment of recurrent pericarditis in the United States, where we derive substantially all of our revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: Revenue figures are stated in the 10-Q statement. The enrollment driver is stated in the 10-K MD&A for 2025 and 2024, and extending it to 2026 is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Growth so far comes from ARCALYST net product revenue, which is the company's only revenue line. Q3 2026 revenue was 285,970 (table in thousands) against 180,855 a year earlier, and nine-month revenue was 743,836 against 475,437. For the continuation, what must be true is that patient enrollment keeps rising, because the 10-K attributes the 2025 and 2024 revenue increases to it.
quotes: The increases in 2025 and 2024 were primarily driven by an increase in patient enrollment.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 8-K earnings release; the Q4 condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The company raised its 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance to $1.045 - $1.050 billion from a prior range of $980 million to $995 million. For this to hold, Q4 sales must continue at the recent run-rate.
quotes: ARCALYST 2026 expected net product revenue increased to $1.045 - $1.050 billion

growth_thesis.basis: Penetration figures are stated in the 8-K. The headroom reading is inferred from the figures.
growth_thesis.claim: Further patient penetration is a stated driver. About 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were on ARCALYST at the end of Q3 2026, and more than 5,450 prescribers have written prescriptions. Growth continues if adoption keeps rising within that core group and therapy duration stays long.
quotes: As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, approximately 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were actively on ARCALYST treatment.

growth_thesis.basis: Patient numbers and the trend toward earlier use are stated in the 10-K. The link to growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Earlier-line use is a second source of headroom. The company says about 26,000 further patients are at their first recurrence, outside the core target population, and that physicians increasingly prescribe ARCALYST earlier. Growth in this group requires continued physician willingness to treat in first recurrence.
quotes: Outside of our core target patient population, there are approximately 26,000 additional patients who are experiencing their first recurrence of the disease.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q statement. The operating-leverage reading is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Earnings have grown faster than revenue so far. Q3 2026 income from operations was 54,236 (table in thousands) against 24,021, and net income was 47,345 against 18,435. This requires revenue to keep outgrowing costs. Collaboration expenses of 105,828 against 63,307 rise with ARCALYST profit because profits are split evenly with Regeneron.
quotes: We evenly split profits on sales of ARCALYST with Regeneron

growth_thesis.basis: The approval and inventory figures are stated. The link to growth is inferred from the risk factor text.
growth_thesis.claim: Supply continuity must hold for sales to keep growing. The FDA approved Samsung as the replacement CDMO in June 2026, ending the earlier status of working to qualify it. Inventory on the balance sheet rose to 108,028 (table in thousands) from 54,895 at year-end.
quotes: in June 2026 the FDA approved Samsung Biologics Co., Ltd.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; its relevance to the growth thesis is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Pricing and coverage must stay favorable. The company says coverage is largely favorable now, and that payor cost controls and 'most favored nation' pricing could reduce net prices or limit access. The evidence does not split revenue growth between volume and price.
quotes: We currently enjoy largely favorable coverage and reimbursement from third party payors for ARCALYST in the approved recurrent pericarditis indication and seek to maintain such favorable coverage and reimbursement.

growth_thesis.basis: Timelines and spending guidance are stated. Any contribution to growth is inferred, and no trial results are in the evidence.
growth_thesis.claim: KPL-387 is the next stated growth source. The Phase 3 PASTORALE trial is enrolling and dosing with data expected in the second half of 2027. The company expects to begin commercializing in 2028 or 2029. This requires positive pivotal data and FDA approval, and R&D spending rises meanwhile.
quotes: We expect data from such trial in the second half of 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures and the expectation are stated. The sufficiency reading is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Funding for the growth plan comes from internal cash generation. Operating cash flow was 144,941 (table in thousands) for nine months, and cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $568.8 million with no debt. This requires the operating plan to stay cash flow positive.
quotes: Kiniksa expects its current operating plan to remain cash flow positive on an annual basis.

material_events.claim: Kiniksa announced that the pivotal Phase 3 trial of KPL-387 in recurrent pericarditis (PASTORALE) had begun enrolling and dosing patients. Data are expected in the second half of 2027, and commercialization is expected in 2028 or 2029.
quotes: In July 2026, we announced that the pivotal Phase 3 trial of KPL-387 in recurrent pericarditis, PASTORALE, had begun enrolling and dosing patients, supported by Phase 2 data at the 300 mg subcutaneous monthly dose level.

risks.claim: The business depends on one product in one country. ARCALYST is the sole product and substantially all revenue is US revenue. Only about 23% of the 14,000 annual multiple-recurrence patients were on treatment at the end of Q3 2026, so growth depends on continued uptake.

While we have realized revenues from such efforts, there is no guarantee that we will be able to maintain the trajectory of growth or significant and sustained revenues in the future.

risks.claim: Payer pricing pressure and price-concession demands could reduce ARCALYST net revenue. The 10-K flags payor cost controls, possible US price-control actions and rebate exposure.
quotes: Any price concessions will reduce our overall revenue generation and may impair the benefit of any price increases we may take.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk list and the 10-Q MD&A; the supply-interruption mechanism is inferred.

in June 2026 the FDA approved Samsung Biologics Co., Ltd.
